learned Additional Government Pleader on behalf of both respondents are before this Court.

2.A counter-affidavit dated 06.02.2019 has been filed by first respondent and in paragraph 1, first respondent has averred that the counter-affidavit is being filed on behalf of second respondent also.
Therefore, both respondents have filed counter-affidavit and pleadings are complete.

3.Main writ petition is now taken up, heard out and is being disposed of.
4.Writ petitioner is manufacturing gingelly oil and is marketing the same under the brand 'CM Gold Palmolein Oil' (hereinafter referred to as 'said oil' for brevity).
http://www.judis.nic.in 5.The first respondent had taken samples of said oil on 23.08.2017 from a store in Melpuram and proceedings under 'The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006' (hereinafter referred to as 'said Act'
for brevity) were commenced.

These proceedings under said Act culminated in an order dated 12.11.2018 bearing Reference Na.Ka.No.1/20377/2018 made by the second respondent which has been called in question in the instant Writ Petition.

This order made by the second respondent which has been called in question in the instant Writ Petition shall hereinafter be referred to as 'impugned order' for the sake of brevity, clarity and convenience.

Though the impugned order does not mention the provision of law under which the same has been made, there is no disputation or disagreement before this Court that the impugned order has been passed by the second respondent under Section 68 of said Act.

Vide impugned order, second respondent has imposed penalties of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand Only) each on the seller and shop owner besides a penalty of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) on the manufacturer.
The seller and shop owner are not before this Court, but the manufacturer on whom a penalty of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) has been imposed vide impugned order is before this Court.
http://www.judis.nic.in
6.Before proceeding further with this matter
, it is to be noted that there is an appeal provision under said Act for assailing the impugned order.

The appeal provision is Section 70 of said Act which reads as follows:
'70. Establishment of Food Safety Appellate Tribunal.

The Central Government or as the case may be, the State Government may, by notification, establish one or more tribunals to be known as the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals from the decisions of the Adjudicating Officer under section 68.

(5) The procedure of appeal and powers of the Tribunal shall be such as may be prescribed by the Central Government.' http://www.judis.nic.in 7.There is no disputation or disagreement before this Court that on the date of filing the instant Writ Petition ie., 22.01.2019, the Appellate Tribunal had not been constituted.

Further, even as of today,
though a Presiding Officer has been appointed to the Appellate Tribunal, the Appellate Tribunal has not commenced sitting.

Therefore, though there is a provision for statutory appeal against the impugned order vide Section 70 of said Act to the Appellate Tribunal, as there is no disputation or disagreement that the Appellate Tribunal had not been constituted on the date of filing of the Writ Petition and is not sitting even as of today, it can be safely inferred that an efficacious or effective alternate remedy is not available to the writ petitioner.
In other words, alternate remedy provided under Section 70 of said Act is in ineffective as of today.
8.Now, reverting to the challenge to the impugned order, learned counsel for writ petitioner assailed the impugned order on three grounds.

In other words, challenge to the impugned order is three fold,
the same can be summarised and set out as follows:
http://www.judis.nic.in a)

The sample was drawn on 23.08.2017 and it was sent to the Food Analyst on the same day by courier, but the Food Analyst ultimately sent the analysis report to the Designated Officer only on 14.12.2017.
Under Section 42(2) of said Act, the report should have been so sent within fourteen days from the date on which the Food Analyst received the sample from the Food Safety Officer.
Therefore, there is a violation of Section 42(2) of said Act which is a mandatory requirement.

b) The complaint being predicated on the report of the Referral Lab dated 07.03.2018 only talks about samples being Substandard and it is nobody's case that it was Misbranded whereas impugned order proceeds on the basis that it is Misbranded.

3 c) Section 49 of said Act provides for parameters for quantification of penalty, but the impugned order is silent about said quantification and there is nothing to show the basis on which, Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) has been imposed as penalty on the writ petitioner.

b) With regard to penalty being imposed on the ground of Misbranding (while complaint is 'Substandard') adverting to the impugned order, it is submitted by the learned state counsel that the impugned order proceeds on the basis that said sample is Substandard, whereas in the concluding paragraph portion alone word 'Misbranded' has been typed which is clearly a typographical error.
It is learned State counsel's submission that writ petitioner is trying to make a mountain out of a mole hill.

The reasons for penalty and http://www.judis.nic.in quantum of penalty have been set out in paragraph No.3 of impugned order (extracted and reproduced supra) and in any event, Section 49 of said Act only adumbrates five different parameters and sub-Section (e) of Section 49 of said Act talks about 'any other relevant factor'.

In the instant case, relevant factors considered by the second respondent vide impugned order have been adumbrated and articulated in paragraph No.3 and there is nothing before this Court to demonstrate that these factors are untenable.
Therefore, last ground of attack, which is taken up first for discussion fails.

14.This Court now takes up the second ground of attack which is predicated on the plea that the impugned order has mulcted the writ petitioner with penalty of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) on the ground of sample being 'Misbranded' whereas the complaint itself is one of said oil being Substandard.
15.Paragraph No.3 of the impugned order has already been extracted, set out supra and alluded to while dealing with Section 49 of said Act.
16.A perusal of paragraph No.3 of the impugned order reveals that http://www.judis.nic.in the order clearly proceeds on the basis of the complaint that the product is Substandard.
All discussions proceed on the basis of Substandard complaint.
Only in the operative portion, the term Misbranded has been used.

Therefore, having read the impugned order in its entirety, this Court has no difficulty in accepting the submission of the State counsel that it is only a typographical error and writ petitioner is trying to make a mountain out of a mole hill.

Therefore, the second ground also fails and this Court has no difficulty in accepting the submission of learned State counsel that the impugned order has been passed on the ground that the product was Substandard and 'Misbranded'
being used in one paragraph is a mere inadvertent typographical error.
17.This
Court now takes up the last ground of attack which has been alluded as first ground in the adumbration supra.
This ground turns on Section 42(2) of said Act.

This Court deems it appropriate to extract 42(2) of said Act and the same reads as follows:
'42. Procedure for launching prosecution.

(2) The Food Analyst after receiving the sample from the Food Safety Officer shall analyse the sample and send the analysis report mentioning method of sampling and analysis within fourteen days to Designated Officer with a copy to http://www.judis.nic.in
Commissioner of Food Safety.'

6 18.The rival submissions extracted supra would reveal that Rule 2.4.2 of said Rules and paragraph 6 are relevant, therefore they are extracted / reproduced and the same read as follows:
'2.4.2. Analysis of food samples by Food Analyst 1.On receipt of the package containing a sample of food for analysis, the Food Analyst or an officer authorized by him shall compare the seals on the container and the outer cover with specimen impression of seal received separately and shall note the condition of the seal thereon.
2.Food laboratories including a mobile food laboratories wherever required, may be established or notified by the Central / State Government for the purpose of testing food samples received from the Food Safety Officer / purchaser.

19.Equally important is sub-paragraph (iii) of paragraph No.5 of the counter affidavit of the respondents which reads as follows:
'5(iii).
The petitioner stated that the second respondent failed to consider that the Food Analyst had not sent report http://www.judis.nic.in within 14 days as contemplated under Section 42.
The Section quoted by him is not relevant and is Section 46(3).

The Food Analyst intimated the reasons for delay in his letter No.0221/2016A4 dated 14.12.2016 addressed the Commissioner for Food Safety under a copy to the Designated Officer, Kanniyakumari District.
This Section also does not prescribe any time limit for informing the reasons for the delay.

Hence the statement of the petitioner cannot be accepted.'
20.In the aforesaid backdrop

, learned counsel for writ petitioner, adverting to the statement of writ petitioner before the second respondent who made the impugned order, pointed out that a plea has been raised before the second respondent regarding violation of Section 42(2) of said Act qua time frame or in other words, plea that the Food Analyst has not sent the report to the Designated Officer within fourteen days from the date of receipt of sample has in fact been raised before the second respondent.

This is articulated in the statement of writ petitioner before the second respondent and the relevant portion reads as follows:
'It is further submitted that the Food Analyst said to have given a report dated 20.12.2017 that the same was Misbranded and Substandard and did not comply with the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
As per Section 42 of the http://www.judis.nic.in Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the report of the Food Analyst shall be sent within 14 days.'
21.Though this point has been raised before the second respondent by writ petitioner with clarity and specificity, the same has not been dealt with by the second respondent in the impugned order.
A perusal of the impugned order reveals that this point has not been dealt with by the second respondent.

22.Besides the plea predicated on paragraph No.6 of Rule 2.4.2 of said Rules, State counsel also submitted that writ petitioner has challenged the report of the Food Analyst dated 14.12.2017 by way of an appeal under Section 46(4) of said Act and the Appellate Authority has on 08.01.2018 made a reference to the Referral Lab which has sent a report dated 07.03.2018 and therefore, writ petitioner cannot now be heard to contend that the Food Analyst has sent the report beyond fourteen days.
In other words, it is the case of State counsel that writ petitioner is estopped from raising this issue after having filed an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst, dated 14.12.2017.

sentences.text: 8 23.This
Court has given its careful consideration to the rival submissions on this aspect of the matter.

With regard to paragraph No.6 of Rule 2.4.2 of the said Rules, the Law is now well settled that an impugned order cannot be improved by way of a counter-affidavit or by way of articulation in the hearing.

In the instant case, the impugned order is completely silent about fourteen days plea predicated on Section 42(2) of said Act, though it has been raised by writ petitioner in his statement with clarity and specificity before the second respondent and therefore sub- paragraph (iii) of paragraph No.5 of the counter-affidavit does not help the respondents in advancing this argument.

With regard to estoppel, though it is not disputed that writ petitioner has filed an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst, the process did not culminate there as the appeal resulted in the matter being referred to the Referral Lab which sent its report on 07.03.2018 on the basis of which impugned order was passed and therefore it is a continuous process culminating in the impugned order.

In this view of the matter, this Court accepts the submission of learned counsel for writ petitioner that writ petitioner is entitled to raise the plea predicated on Section 42(2) of said Act, in the instant Writ Petition now.

This is more so, owing to the peculiar facts and circumstances of this case where the impugned order is silent about the plea though the same has been raised http://www.judis.nic.in with clarity and specificity by writ petitioner in his statement before the second respondent in the course of impugned order being passed.

24.One factor which has weighed in the mind of this Court is that time lines prescribed qua said Act appear to be time lines which are intended to ensure that the product which is tested does not become stale.
In the instant case, the date of manufacture of the product is August, 2017.

This Court is conscious of the fact that six months period expired only in February 2018, but what is of relevance is the mandatory requirement under Section 42(2) of said Act so designed to ensure expediency in testing and deciding.

Though time line qua Section 42(2) of said Act is not non-negotiable in the light of paragraph 6 of Rule 2.4.2 of said Rules, though there is some material in the counter-affidavit and though delay has been explained, it has not been articulated in the impugned order.

In the light of the settled position that an impugned order cannot be improved by way of a counter-affidavit and in the light of peculiar facts and circumstances of this case, this Court is inclined to sustain this submission of writ petitioner predicated on time line qua Section 42(2) of said Act.
25.In the result
, it follows as an inevitable sequitur that the impugned http://www.judis.nic.in order deserves to be set aside and the impugned order is set aside.
Instant Writ Petition is allowed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
